analysis.title: The Wolfe Power Trip: Q3 Commodities Recap; Not so spooky season (October 12, 2026)
key_insights: Wolfe raises its IPP sentiment meter two notches to 4. The CEG/GOOGL deal revived the independent power producers after a broader AI sell-off at the end of the prior week.

CEG signed two data center contracts at the conference. AMZN at Calvert Cliffs covers 690 MWs (500 MWs existing plus 190 MWs uprates). GOOGL covers 3.6 GWs (2.7 GWs existing plus 890 MWs uprates). Wolfe reads this as proof that existing generation can still be contracted despite PJM reliability backstop procurement (RBP) cost and IRAS curtailment risks.
TLN announced Mac's retirement with Terry becoming CEO, plus a $1.5B accelerated share repurchase.

FERC ruled on the PJM RBP at the last minute. It accepted most of PJM's proposal but sent back potentially unjust areas such as cost allocation. PJM plans a 205 filing by 10/29 and FERC then has 60 days to rule, which pushes central procurement into early 2027. The overall procurement size of 6.8 GWs appears to be shrinking as CEG's newly contracted MWs offset it.

FERC rejected all of PJM's IRAS proposal except the large load registry. It rejected curtailment ahead of demand response and the exclusion of new load from auctions, and found the plan would have disrupted existing commercial arrangements.
CEG remains Wolfe's top pick among the IPPs, followed by VST.

Wolfe estimates CEG is now about 35% contracted on an EPS basis at full ramp in 2032, the highest among the IPPs. The figure rests on the existing MWs of CEG's three recent deals, which total 4.1 GWs. Including the nuclear PTC floor, nearly half of CEG's total earnings are contracted.

Wolfe estimates 45% of CEG's carbon-free fleet is contracted on a TWh basis. Its earlier estimates put TLN at low-30s% of FCF, then mid-20s% now, VST at low-20s% of EBITDA and NRG with very little contracted.

Wolfe's CEG contract math assumes the AMZN and GOOGL deals were signed at a $5/MWh premium to the energy curve plus capacity. That implies about $95/MWh for AMZN in the BGE basis and about $77/MWh for GOOGL, assuming half the volume is at PJM-West and half at NI Hub. The 890 MWs of GOOGL uprates is treated as an unknown.
Wolfe's thesis is that long-term contracts with high-quality counterparties at premium prices raise both earnings and the multiple as IPPs move closer to infrastructure plays.
From mid-January to early August there were no contracted deals in the IPP space. CEG has announced three since its Q2 call two months earlier.
PJM led power prices higher in Q3 after an all-time peak load of 168 GWs in July. Real-time prices spiked above $1,000/MWh several times in the quarter. Q3 average spot was $68/MWh, up 49% YoY.
PJM-West forwards rose $6/$8/$10 from Q2-end for 2026/2027/2028. The curve is still backwardated but less steep, with 2026 in the mid-$80s/MWh and 2027/2028 in the mid-$70s/MWh.
Since Q2 earnings, PJM power is up about 10% to $74/$77 per MWh for 2027/2028 and sparks are up about 20% to $48/MWh. PJM is now less backwardated until 2029.

ERCOT prices continued to fall despite a hot summer and a record peak load, because renewables and storage absorbed the load. Q3 spot was $32-36/MWh, down 0-5% YoY in Houston, North and South and down 11% in West.

ERCOT forwards fell 10-14% for 2026/2027 and 7-10% for 2028, and the curve is in sharp contango. Since Q2 earnings, ERCOT power is down 6% to $42/MWh (2027) and $47/MWh (2028), and sparks are down 7% (2027) and 10% (2028) to $21-22/MWh.

Weak ERCOT real-time pricing and Batch Zero delays have weighed on the near-term forward curve. Wolfe still sees ERCOT fundamentals as strong long term, with 63 GWs of base load in Batch Zero planned by 2030 on a 91 GW peak load grid. ERCOT's final Batch Zero base load number is due in its December 10 report to the PUCT.

Other regions moved less. New England spot was up 5-6% YoY and West spot up 5-12%. New England forwards were down 4% for 2026 and up 3%/6% for 2027/2028. West forwards were up 8-10% for 2026, 6-9% for 2027 and 2-4% for 2028. New York forwards were up 2-7%.
Spot natural gas averaged $2.89/MMBtu in Q3, down 18% YoY. NYMEX forwards moved up 4% for 2026, down 3% for 2027 and up 3% for 2028 versus Q2. PRB coal was flat at $14.70/ton.

PJM has struggled to attract new supply because regulatory noise raises private investment hurdle rates. Wolfe believes hyperscalers prefer bilateral offtake deals over the central RBP procurement, and says basically all PJM nuclear uprates it knows of are sold out except at PEG's fleet.

Market forward power prices sit above Wolfe's published assumptions in PJM West by 6.7% (2026), 14.6% (2027) and 18.6% (2028). ERCOT market prices are 5-11% below Wolfe's assumptions across 2026-2028.

Wolfe's 2026/2027/2028 estimates versus consensus: CEG EPS $12.14/$13.18/$16.76 against consensus $12.06/$13.31/$16.82. VST EBITDA $7,291M/$7,945M/$8,489M against consensus $7,283M/$8,109M/$8,850M. TLN EBITDA $2,193M/$2,767M/$3,048M against consensus $2,134M/$2,729M/$2,968M. NRG EBITDA $5,549M/$5,915M/$6,136M against consensus $5,510M/$6,087M/$6,512M.

IPP valuation: the average two-year-forward mark-to-market EV/EBITDA is 8.7x against a historical average of 7.8x. CEG trades at 24.6x/22.6x 2026/2027 P/E versus the S&P 500 at 21.5x/18.6x, and NRG at 12.3x/10.6x.

Wolfe's CEG valuation embeds a 50% chance of a $30/MWh premium to the nuclear PTC floor. Its 2028 EPS sensitivity is $5.51 (33%) to a $10/MWh nuclear attribute premium and $2.26 (13%) to raising the PTC inflation adder from 2% to 3%.

Regulatory calendar: PJM 205 filing on RBP revisions by 10/29, PJM stakeholder meeting on cost allocation 10/22, PJM large load registry compliance filing by 11/8, state comments on long-term capacity reform 10/15, PJM RBP target posting 11/18, ERCOT Batch Zero eligibility report 12/10, and 2029/2030 PJM capacity auction results 12/22.
VST's $4.0B Cogentrix acquisition (5.5 GW across PJM, New England and ERCOT) received FERC approval on 8/5. DoJ approval remains and the close is expected in late 2026.

The 2028/2029 PJM capacity auction cleared at the $325/MW-day cap, 6.8 GW short of the reliability requirement, and would have priced at $555/MW-day uncapped. The 2029/2030 auction in December is the last with the collar in place.
Government-backed gas build announcements continue: $66B U.S./Japan for 18.7 GW and a $22B U.S./South Korea project (Project Star) for 6.5 GW in Texas, with NEE developing and operating for a fee.

market_movers.rationale: CEG stays top of Wolfe's IPP ranking after the AMZN and GOOGL contracts. About 35% of its EPS outlook is now contracted at full ramp, the highest among IPPs.
VST ranks second behind CEG in Wolfe's IPP pecking order. Its FERC-approved Cogentrix acquisition awaits DoJ approval.
TLN announced a CEO transition and a $1.5B accelerated share repurchase. Wolfe estimates its contracted share of FCF fell to mid-20s% because PJM power and sparks improved the overall outlook.
NRG still has very little contracted while it awaits its first big data center deal.

sector_views.rationale: Sentiment meter raised to 4. Long-term premium-priced contracts with hyperscalers lift earnings visibility and move IPPs toward infrastructure-style multiples.
The report covers PEG estimates and regulated comps in tables. Regulated utilities trade at an average 17.3x 2026 P/E and 3.6% dividend yield, with no stated directional call.

earnings_insights: Wolfe CEG EPS estimates (not reported results): 2026 $12.14, 2027 $13.18, 2028 $16.76, versus consensus $12.06, $13.31, $16.82. Mark-to-market EPS is $12.40, $13.60, $17.45.
Wolfe CEG base EPS (PTC floor plus historical retail margins) estimates are $6.22 (2026), $7.39 (2027), $10.33 (2028). Base plus enhanced EPS equals the published estimates.
Wolfe NRG EBITDA estimates: $5,549M (2026), $5,915M (2027), $6,136M (2028) against consensus $5,510M, $6,087M, $6,512M. Wolfe EPS estimates are $8.76, $10.18, $11.27.
Wolfe VST EBITDA estimates: $7,291M, $7,945M, $8,489M against consensus $7,283M, $8,109M, $8,850M. Wolfe FCF estimates are $4,052M, $4,667M, $5,211M.
Wolfe TLN EBITDA estimates: $2,193M, $2,767M, $3,048M against consensus $2,134M, $2,729M, $2,968M. Wolfe FCF estimates are $1,333M, $1,728M, $2,007M.
Wolfe PEG EPS estimates: $4.37 (2026), $4.66 (2027), $5.00 (2028) against consensus $4.37, $4.67, $5.01. The regulated segment is 75% of 2026 earnings.
Hedge levels assumed by Wolfe for 2026/2027/2028: NRG 75%/38%/13%, PEG 95%/75%/50%, TLN 84%/75%/35%, VST 100%/95%/75%. CEG is primarily hedged via the nuclear PTC floor.
TLN announced a $1.5B accelerated share repurchase and a CEO transition at the conference.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Tight PJM supply and record load keep spot prices high, which supports merchant generator earnings in the region.
Record demand against little new supply tightens the grid into the fall.
Forwards keep setting new highs and the curve is less backwardated, which raises the mark-to-market value of unhedged generation.

macro_indicators.reading: $32-36/MWh across zones, down 0-5% YoY in Houston, North and South and 11% in West
macro_indicators.interpretation: Renewables and storage absorbed record load, so prices did not rise.
Weak real-time pricing and Batch Zero delay uncertainty weigh on the near-term curve, which remains in contango.

macro_indicators.indicator: Henry Hub / NYMEX natural gas spot
macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower gas prices widen spark spreads for gas generators when power prices hold.
The auction cleared 6.8 GW short of the reliability requirement, which signals continued scarcity.

risk_factors: PJM's compliance filing and FERC's 60-day review of the RBP revisions could push central procurement into early 2027 and keep regulatory uncertainty elevated.
Customers like GOOGL accepted RBP cost and IRAS curtailment risks, so those regulatory design choices still affect contracted pricing.
ERCOT Batch Zero delays and data center verification create near-term uncertainty over load growth, with the final base load number due December 10.
ERCOT forwards remain in sharp contango and near-term prices are falling, which hurts ERCOT-heavy generators.
New MWs from uprates come with unquantified capex that would require cash usage or debt issuance, which Wolfe excludes from its contracted-earnings math.
Wolfe's percent-contracted figures rest on assumed contract premiums ($5/MWh) and an assumed 50/50 split between NI Hub and PJM-West for the GOOGL volumes.
State-level affordability politics, including New Jersey bill sensitivity and Texas data center cost rules, could constrain data center economics.
charts_described: Exhibit 7 plots the IPP average two-year-forward mark-to-market EV/EBITDA from 2010 to 2026 and labels the current (10/9/26) reading at 8.7x against a historical average of 7.8x.
vol_and_positioning: Wolfe notes a broader AI sell-off at the end of the prior week, while the CEG/GOOGL deal lifted the IPP stocks.
IPP average two-year-forward mark-to-market EV/EBITDA is 8.7x versus a historical average of 7.8x as of 10/9/26.
geopolitical: The White House and Japan announced a $66B investment in three gas plants totaling 18.7 GW, and the U.S. Department of Commerce announced a fourth 6.5 GW Texas project (Project Star) backed by $22B from South Korea.
The White House and PJM state governors pushed PJM toward an emergency reliability procurement with hyperscalers bidding on 15-year contracts.

tension_points.bull_case: Wolfe sees strong long-term ERCOT fundamentals, with 63 GWs of base load in Batch Zero planned by 2030 on a 91 GW peak load grid.
tension_points.bear_case: Spot prices keep falling despite record peak load, Batch Zero delays create near-term uncertainty, and forwards are down 10-14% for 2026/2027 with the curve in sharp contango.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ERCOT's final Batch Zero base load number in its December 10 report to the PUCT.
